objective: Generate P99.4 R0005 to complete the global Pepper visual identity and design-system implementation so the rendered Pepper application no longer presents visually as a lightly rebranded Hermes interface. R0004 remains valid historical evidence, but R0005 supersedes it as the current material revision because the accepted R0004 candidate did not fully satisfy the intended product-level visual result. R0005 must use fresh current canonical source authority at expected HEAD a016bb9d36d84745acf5a84a3a9e8690a87be178, not R0004 scratch candidate bytes, and must stop at pending approval with no execution.
context: Current workflow is awaiting_material_revision for P99.4 after durable post-accept material-revision request authority. R0004 review is accepted_historical and its human Git handoff is superseded_by_material_revision; do not reinterpret or mutate R0004 history.

Material revision classification is MATERIAL_VISUAL_SCOPE_INCOMPLETE. R0004 introduced useful branding infrastructure, but its visible delta was too small and still inherited Hermes green/turquoise product identity.

Pepper visual target: elegant, dark, professional, restrained, technically sophisticated, premium, engineering-oriented, information-dense without clutter, and clearly distinct from upstream Hermes. It must not feel like a Hermes dashboard with only a small Pepper badge added.

Primary surfaces must be dominated by black, near-black, charcoal, graphite, and dark neutral gray. Pepper blue is a restrained product accent for selected navigation, active tabs, primary actions, focus treatment, brand mark, controlled highlights, selected data, and links where appropriate. Do not flood the UI with blue.

Semantic colors remain distinct: success/approved green, warning/pending amber/yellow, error/failed/rejected/blocked red, informational Pepper blue or neutral informational tone as appropriate. Do not replace semantic green with Pepper blue.

Pepper belongs visually to the Siamese family through dark neutral surfaces, restrained blue highlights, premium technical language, compact brand treatment, and disciplined component styling. Do not insert the Siamese cat logo unless separately authorized.
Dark mode is the primary acceptance target; light-mode infrastructure must not be broken. Full light-mode parity is not required.

Known unrelated untracked C64 path is not part of R0005 and must not be deleted, modified, staged, included in scope, or used as evidence: 2_products/pepper-agent/tests/hermes_cli/test_c64_validation_authority_boundary.py

Add or update reusable semantic tokens for dark neutral surfaces, Pepper blue accents, semantic status colors, focus rings, borders, elevation, spacing, radii, typography, and interaction states.

constraints: Pepper-specific brand/accent tokens must not simply map to var(--color-primary) if that value remains Hermes turquoise; final rendered Pepper accent must be Pepper blue.

Audit and replace inherited green/turquoise product-brand styling in primary theme tokens, navigation selection, active states, buttons, links, focus rings, borders, highlights, badges, shell accents, icon accents, hover states, terminal/chat decoration, and card decoration, while preserving green for semantic success.

Apply the Pepper visual system to global background, top/title bar, left sidebar, navigation sections, selected navigation state, hover state, separators, footer/system area, main content surface, panel boundaries, and right-side/context surfaces where shared architecture supports them.

Sidebar is a primary acceptance surface: near-black/charcoal background, restrained section hierarchy, subdued inactive items, Pepper-blue selected state, coherent hover states, neutral inactive icons, controlled separators, clear Pepper branding, reduced Hermes visual language, and preserved CONTROL, WORK, AGENTS, AUTOMATION, RESOURCES, SYSTEM sections/routes.
Content surfaces must use a hierarchy of dark surfaces rather than one flat black surface: canvas, panel, elevated panel, interactive surface, selected surface.

Interaction states must be coherent and reusable: default, hover, active, selected, focused, disabled, loading, pending, success, warning, failed, rejected, blocked. Important semantic states must not rely only on color; use combinations of text, icon, border, label, chip, marker, shape, and color.
Buttons and controls must clearly distinguish primary Pepper-blue actions, destructive red actions, disabled state, and visible focus on dark surfaces.

Structural design system must establish consistent radii, borders, separators, elevation, shadows, selected outlines, active rings, spacing hierarchy, and sizing hierarchy with premium restrained technical character, avoiding excessive glow, neon, thick outlines, gratuitous glassmorphism, large decorative gradients, and visual noise.

Typography must preserve high information density and technical readability across product title, page headings, section headings, card titles, body, metadata, status, and monospace technical values without unnecessarily replacing the existing font stack.

Pepper brand lockup must preserve compatible R0004 concepts while making PEPPER the primary identity and Hermes/upstream provenance secondary; Pepper mark must use Pepper blue, not inherited Hermes turquoise.

Preserve or improve readable text/background contrast, visible focus, non-color-only status meaning, accessible labels, decorative aria-hidden marks, disabled-state legibility, responsive behavior, desktop control-plane density, compact navigation, technical metadata readability, and panel layout behavior.
